description: Condition Index: an editorial indicator, not a scientific one. Each signal is placed on a 0–100 scale between a 'calm' value (0) and an 'alarm' value (100), clipped at both ends. The index is the weighted average of the signals that have data; missing signals are left out and the remaining weights are rescaled.

signals.name: Conflict in the news
signals.explain: Share of events coded by GDELT in the last 24 hours that are 'material conflict' (assaults, fighting, mass violence). Uses GDELT's 15-minute event files only. Calm 10% and alarm 16% are our choice: in recent days the daily share has been about 12–14%.

signals.name: Deaths in organised violence
signals.explain: Deaths recorded by UCDP in the latest available month (candidate events, 'best' estimate). Calm 5,000 and alarm 25,000 a month are our choice: 25,000 a month is about 300,000 a year, above the highest yearly battle-death total since 1989 (about 285,000 in 2022, which counts only state-based conflict).

signals.name: Significant earthquakes
signals.explain: Earthquakes the USGS classes as significant in the last 7 days (combines magnitude, damage and felt reports). Calm 1 and alarm 8 a week are our choice: 8 means more than one a day.

signals.name: Active storms and volcanoes
signals.explain: Severe storms and active volcanoes open in NASA EONET. Wildfires are left out: there are always dozens and they would swamp the signal. Calm 2 and alarm 15 open events are our choice.

signals.name: Pace of job cuts citing AI
signals.explain: Last month's US job cuts where companies cited AI (Challenger), divided by the average of the months before it (up to 12). 1 means a normal pace. Calm 0.8 (below the usual pace) and alarm 2.0 (double it) are our choice. Weighted 10, like the earthquake and storm signals and half the conflict-news signal, because the reason is the companies' own.
